## Overview

Supervised learning learns from examples where the answer is already known, such as
hauls where the catch was recorded or images where a specialist named the species, and
then predicts the answer where it is unknown. Most marine work needs this family of
methods. The section introduces one method per page, from linear regression, the
yardstick for everything after, through models for counts and for yes-or-no answers, to
k-nearest neighbours, decision trees, random forests and boosting. All of them run on
the same simulated survey, so each new method can be compared with the ones before it,
and the last page narrows the choice between them.

## Further resources

**Documentation**

- [Build a model](https://www.tidymodels.org/start/models/), tidymodels. One model specification, several engines.
- [Search parsnip models](https://www.tidymodels.org/find/parsnip/), tidymodels. Which methods have a `parsnip` interface and what each engine needs.
- [Supervised learning](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/supervised_learning.html), scikit-learn user guide. The whole menu, with [linear models](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/linear_model.html) and [ensembles](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/ensemble.html) as the two that matter here.
